igcse-0580-manipulation-collect-like-ter.description: Recognise the algebraic part of each term, carry signs correctly and simplify expressions with powers and mixed terms.

sections.title: Which terms can go together?
sections.label: Match the algebraic parts
sections.intro: A term has a coefficient and an algebraic part. To decide what can be combined, compare the algebraic parts first.

blocks.html: Sort by the letters and their powers. Change only the coefficient when you combine a group.

figure.alt: Matching shapes share the same group. Different shapes move to distinct groups.
figure.caption: Terms in the same group have identical algebraic parts.

blocks.title: Collect terms with the same algebraic part
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(26 x+24 y+11 x+6 y\). Enter the simplified coefficient for each listed group. Use 0 if a group cancels.
blocks.hint: Only combine terms with the same letters raised to the same powers.
blocks.solution:
Group matching algebraic parts, keeping the sign attached to each term.

\(26 x+11 x+24 y+6 y\).

Combine the coefficient groups. \(\left(26+11\right)x+\left(24+6\right)y=37 x + 30 y\).

blocks.html: \(5x+4y\) already has unlike terms. Combining the coefficient numbers would change the expression.

blocks.title: Collect terms with the same algebraic part
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(- 8 x-11+x- 16 x+4\). Enter the simplified coefficient for each listed group. Use 0 if a group cancels.
blocks.hint: Only combine terms with the same letters raised to the same powers.
blocks.solution:
Group matching algebraic parts, keeping the sign attached to each term.

\(- 8 x+x- 16 x-11+4\).

Combine the coefficient groups. \(\left(-8+1-16\right)x+\left(-11+4\right)=- 23 x - 7\).

blocks.html: Keep a subtraction sign attached to the term that follows it.

sections.title: What if the letters or powers look different?
sections.label: Check powers and order
sections.intro: Multiplication can be reordered within a term. Changing a power changes the term.

blocks.html: \(xy=yx\), so those terms can combine. The terms \(x^2\) and \(x\) have different powers and stay separate.

blocks.title: Collect terms with the same algebraic part
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(25 x^{2}- 23 x- 10 x^{2}- 15 x\). Enter the simplified coefficient for each listed group. Use 0 if a group cancels.
blocks.hint: Only combine terms with the same letters raised to the same powers.
blocks.solution:
Group matching algebraic parts, keeping the sign attached to each term.

\(25 x^{2}- 10 x^{2}- 23 x- 15 x\).

Combine the coefficient groups. \(\left(25-10\right)x^{2}+\left(-23-15\right)x=15 x^{2} - 38 x\).

blocks.html: A term with two letters and a term with just one letter do not become like terms because they share one letter.

blocks.title: Collect terms with the same algebraic part
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(5 x y+20 y+15 x y- 7 x+3\). Enter the simplified coefficient for each listed group. Use 0 if a group cancels.
blocks.hint: Only combine terms with the same letters raised to the same powers.
blocks.solution:
Group matching algebraic parts, keeping the sign attached to each term.

\(5 x y+15 x y+20 y- 7 x+3\).

Combine the coefficient groups. \(\left(5+15\right)x y+\left(20\right)y+\left(-7\right)x+\left(3\right)=20 x y - 7 x + 20 y + 3\).

blocks.html: Write each mixed term with the letters in a consistent order.

sections.title: How do I handle constants and cancellation?
sections.label: Keep the signed totals
sections.intro: You can collect one group at a time and then write all the resulting non-zero terms together.

blocks.html: Collect constants with constants. If a group’s coefficient adds to zero, leave that group out of the answer.

blocks.title: Collect terms with the same algebraic part
blocks.prompt: Simplify \(24 x^{2}+22 y+20- 24 x^{2}- 14 y\). Enter the simplified coefficient for each listed group. Use 0 if a group cancels.
blocks.hint: Only combine terms with the same letters raised to the same powers.

blocks.html: A pair such as \(8x^2-8x^2\) contributes zero. Its cancellation does not affect other terms.

Combine the coefficient groups. \(\left(4-1-2\right)x+\left(9+6\right)y+\left(14\right)=x + 15 y + 14\).

blocks.html: Check whether a coefficient of 1 or −1 can be written without the digit 1.

igcse-0580-manipulation-single-brackets.description: Distribute a signed number or monomial through one bracket, then collect any like terms that remain.

sections.title: What does the outside factor multiply?
sections.label: Distribute to every inside term
sections.intro: A rectangle with a common height can be split by width. The sum of the smaller areas is the full product.

blocks.html: \(a(b+c)=ab+ac\). Work through the terms one at a time.

figure.alt: One rectangle with a common height is split into three areas by two vertical lines.
figure.caption: One outside factor multiplies each part inside the bracket.

blocks.title: Distribute the outside factor
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(18\left(24 x+17\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Give every inside term its own multiplication. Include each sign.
blocks.solution:
Multiply the outside factor by every term inside its bracket.

The products are \(432 x+306\).

The simplified result is \(432 x + 306\).

sections.title: What if the outside factor contains a sign or a letter?
sections.label: Multiply the signs and algebra
sections.intro: For each product, decide the numerical sign first. Then multiply its letters.

blocks.html: Keep signed coefficients together. When the same letter is multiplied by itself, its powers add.

blocks.title: Distribute the outside factor
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(- 23 x\left(17 x- 16 y\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Give every inside term its own multiplication. Include each sign.
blocks.solution:
Multiply the outside factor by every term inside its bracket.

The products are \(- 391 x^{2}+368 x y\).

The simplified result is \(- 391 x^{2} + 368 x y\).

blocks.html: For example, \((-3y)(-2y)=6y^2\). Two negative factors give a positive term.

blocks.hint: Give every inside term its own multiplication. Include each sign.

The products are \(- 110 x y- 220 y^{2}- 462 y\).

The simplified result is \(- 110 x y - 220 y^{2} - 462 y\).

blocks.html: Write signs in the intermediate products before combining any like terms.

sections.title: How do I simplify after two separate expansions?
sections.label: Expand, then collect
sections.intro: When expressions are added or subtracted, treat their outside factors as signed numbers or monomials.

blocks.html: Expand each single bracket. A minus immediately before a bracket applies to the whole bracket.

blocks.title: Distribute the outside factor
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(16\left(22 x+15\right)-4\left(x-15\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Give every inside term its own multiplication. Include each sign.
blocks.solution:
Expand each bracket separately. The sign before a bracket belongs to its outside factor.

Expand to \(352 x+240- 4 x+60\) before collecting like terms.

The simplified result is \(348 x + 300\).

blocks.html: A minus before the second bracket changes the sign of each term from that bracket.

igcse-0580-manipulation-double-brackets.description: Find all four products, combine the middle terms and explain what changes in a squared bracket.

sections.title: How do I keep track of all four products?
sections.label: Place signs in a grid
sections.intro: A multiplication grid lets you see which two terms produced each cell.

blocks.html: Each of two signed terms multiplies both signed terms in the other bracket. Record all four outcomes.

figure.alt: An area rectangle is divided into two rows and two columns. The four resulting pieces are highlighted individually.
figure.caption: A two-by-two multiplication grid records all four products.

blocks.title: Expand a product of two brackets
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(x + 24\right)\left(x + 18\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Each term in one bracket must multiply each term in the other.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(x\)\(18\)
\(x\)\(x^{2}\)\(18 x\)
\(24\)\(24 x\)\(432\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(x^{2}+18 x+24 x+432=x^{2} + 42 x + 432\).

blocks.html: Starting with the two first terms and the two last terms misses the two cross-products.

blocks.title: Expand a product of two brackets
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(4 x - 6\right)\left(x + 23\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Each term in one bracket must multiply each term in the other.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(x\)\(23\)
\(4 x\)\(4 x^{2}\)\(92 x\)
\(-6\)\(- 6 x\)\(-138\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(4 x^{2}+92 x- 6 x-138=4 x^{2} + 86 x - 138\).

blocks.html: Check the leading coefficient using the two variable terms and the constant using the two constants.

sections.title: How do I expand a squared bracket?
sections.label: Repeat both terms
sections.intro: The two cross-products match when the brackets match, so add both of them.

blocks.html: Rewrite the square as two identical factors. Both off-diagonal cells still contribute.

blocks.title: Expand a product of two brackets
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(7 x - 23\right)\left(4 x + 17\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Each term in one bracket must multiply each term in the other.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(4 x\)\(17\)
\(7 x\)\(28 x^{2}\)\(119 x\)
\(-23\)\(- 92 x\)\(-391\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(28 x^{2}+119 x- 92 x-391=28 x^{2} + 27 x - 391\).

blocks.html: \((x+4)^2\) has a middle term. Squaring the terms separately omits it.

blocks.title: Expand a product of two brackets
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(3 x + 5\right)^2\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Each term in one bracket must multiply each term in the other.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(3 x\)\(5\)
\(3 x\)\(9 x^{2}\)\(15 x\)
\(5\)\(15 x\)\(25\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(9 x^{2}+15 x+15 x+25=9 x^{2} + 30 x + 25\).

blocks.html: Check the sign of the cross-term in a square containing a minus sign.

sections.title: When can the middle terms cancel?
sections.label: Keep opposite signs
sections.intro: Work out the two cross-products explicitly. They can reinforce or cancel each other.

blocks.html: Two cross-products of the same magnitude and opposite sign add to zero. Only omit the middle term after checking that cancellation.

blocks.title: Expand a product of two brackets
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(6 x + 22\right)\left(6 x - 22\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Each term in one bracket must multiply each term in the other.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(6 x\)\(-22\)
\(6 x\)\(36 x^{2}\)\(- 132 x\)
\(22\)\(132 x\)\(-484\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(36 x^{2}- 132 x+132 x-484=36 x^{2} - 484\).

blocks.html: Two opposite constant signs do not guarantee cancellation when the variable coefficients differ.

blocks.title: Expand a product of two brackets
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(4 - 2 x\right)\left(8 x + 21\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Each term in one bracket must multiply each term in the other.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(8 x\)\(21\)
\(4\)\(32 x\)\(84\)
\(- 2 x\)\(- 16 x^{2}\)\(- 42 x\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(32 x+84- 16 x^{2}- 42 x=- 16 x^{2} - 10 x + 84\).

blocks.html: A negative variable coefficient multiplies every term in the other bracket.

\(24\)\(120 x\)\(-432\)
Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(40 x^{2}- 144 x+120 x-432=40 x^{2} - 24 x - 432\).

solution: Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

\(6\)\(24 x\)\(36\)

revision.body:
Methods

StepWhat to do
Place signs in a gridEach of two signed terms multiplies both signed terms in the other bracket. Record all four outcomes.
Repeat both termsRewrite the square as two identical factors. Both off-diagonal cells still contribute.
Keep opposite signsTwo cross-products of the same magnitude and opposite sign add to zero. Only omit the middle term after checking that cancellation.

Worked line

\((3x-2)(x+5)=3x^2+13x-10\)

Check yourself

Expand and simplify \((2x-3)^2\).

Answer \(4x^2-12x+9\)
revision.checks:
• Starting with the two first terms and the two last terms misses the two cross-products.
  • \((x+4)^2\) has a middle term. Squaring the terms separately omits it.
  • Two opposite constant signs do not guarantee cancellation when the variable coefficients differ.
revision.examTip: A negative variable coefficient multiplies every term in the other bracket.

igcse-0580-manipulation-common-factors.description: Find the complete highest common monomial factor and check the remaining bracket by re-expansion.

sections.title: How do I find the highest common number?
sections.label: Compare all coefficients
sections.intro: Factorising reverses distribution. The same factor must divide every term.

blocks.html: Use the highest common factor of the magnitudes of all coefficients. You may keep a positive coefficient outside.

figure.alt: Three groups have the same marked prefix. Each has a different remaining component.
figure.caption: Identify the part shared by every term, then keep the different quotients together.

blocks.title: Extract the whole common factor
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully by extracting the highest common factor from \(144 x + 8\). Give the highest common monomial factor with a positive coefficient, then the expression inside the bracket.
blocks.hint: Take the lowest shared power of each letter and the highest common factor of the numerical coefficients.
blocks.solution:
Find what divides every coefficient and every term’s algebraic part. Here that gives \(8\).

Divide each term by \(8\) and put the quotients in one bracket.

\(144 x + 8=8\left(18 x + 1\right)\). Expand the product to check it.

blocks.html: A factor that divides only the first coefficient is not shared.

blocks.title: Extract the whole common factor
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully by extracting the highest common factor from \(8 x^{2} - 88 x\). Give the highest common monomial factor with a positive coefficient, then the expression inside the bracket.

Divide each term by \(8 x\) and put the quotients in one bracket.

\(8 x^{2} - 88 x=8 x\left(x - 11\right)\). Expand the product to check it.

blocks.html: Multiply the bracket back by the common factor as a final check.

sections.title: Which letters belong outside the bracket?
sections.label: Find the smallest shared powers
sections.intro: The highest common monomial combines a numerical factor and any shared powers of letters.

blocks.html: A variable can go outside to the lowest power that appears in every term. If one term does not contain a letter, its shared power is zero.

blocks.html: Put all the shared numerical and variable factors outside, then divide.

sections.title: How do I tell whether the factorisation is complete?
sections.label: Check every quotient
sections.intro: Look at three-term expressions in exactly the same way. A factor must be present in all three terms.

blocks.html: Divide each term by the whole common factor and keep the original relative signs. The bracket should have no common factor left besides 1.

blocks.prompt: Factorise fully by extracting the highest common factor from \(96 x^{2} + 12 x y + 6 x\). Give the highest common monomial factor with a positive coefficient, then the expression inside the bracket.

igcse-0580-manipulation-extended-product.description: Expand products with two letters and extend the multiplication method to three or more brackets.

sections.title: What changes if both brackets have two different letters?
sections.label: Retain each algebraic part
sections.intro: The grid method still lists all four products. The letters tell you which terms are like.

blocks.html: Multiply as usual. Combine the \(xy\) terms together and retain the \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) terms separately.

figure.alt: A sequence of three boxes shows an initial pair of brackets, its product and multiplication by the remaining bracket.
figure.caption: Keep track of the unused bracket when expanding in stages.

blocks.title: Expand brackets containing two different letters
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(8 x + 24 y\right)\left(5 x + 18 y\right)\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Keep the two letters separate. Products xy and yx have the same algebraic part.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(5 x\)\(18 y\)
\(8 x\)\(40 x^{2}\)\(144 x y\)
\(24 y\)\(120 x y\)\(432 y^{2}\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(40 x^{2}+144 x y+120 x y+432 y^{2}=40 x^{2} + 264 x y + 432 y^{2}\).

blocks.html: \(x^2,xy,y^2\) are three different algebraic parts.

blocks.title: Expand brackets containing two different letters
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(6 x - 6 y\right)^2\). Write the expanded expression.
blocks.hint: Keep the two letters separate. Products xy and yx have the same algebraic part.
blocks.solution:
Place one bracket across the top and the other down the side. Multiply each row label by each column label.

×\(6 x\)\(- 6 y\)
\(6 x\)\(36 x^{2}\)\(- 36 x y\)
\(- 6 y\)\(- 36 x y\)\(36 y^{2}\)

Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(36 x^{2}- 36 x y- 36 x y+36 y^{2}=36 x^{2} - 72 x y + 36 y^{2}\).

blocks.html: In a square with two letters, include both cross-products.

sections.title: How can I expand three brackets without losing terms?
sections.label: Expand one pair first
sections.intro: You can choose any pair first. A convenient pair may have fewer terms in its expanded product.

blocks.html: Multiply two brackets and simplify their product. Then multiply every term of that product by every term in the third bracket.

blocks.title: Expand three or more brackets in stages
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(x - 23\right)\left(x + 17\right)\left(x + 16\right)\). Write the fully expanded result.
blocks.hint: Combine the first two brackets, then use their expanded product with the next bracket.
blocks.solution:
Expand the first two brackets. \(\left(x - 23\right)\left(x + 17\right)=x^{2} - 6 x - 391\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(x^{2} - 6 x - 391\right)\left(x + 16\right)=x^{3} + 10 x^{2} - 487 x - 6256\).

blocks.html: A quadratic result after the first multiplication is intermediate. One bracket is still unused.

blocks.title: Expand three or more brackets in stages
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(5 x + 5\right)\left(x - 22\right)\left(6 x + 21\right)\). Write the fully expanded result.
blocks.hint: Combine the first two brackets, then use their expanded product with the next bracket.
blocks.solution:
Expand the first two brackets. \(\left(5 x + 5\right)\left(x - 22\right)=5 x^{2} - 105 x - 110\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(5 x^{2} - 105 x - 110\right)\left(6 x + 21\right)=30 x^{3} - 525 x^{2} - 2865 x - 2310\).

blocks.html: Keep a record of the brackets that have already been expanded.

sections.title: What if a factor repeats or there are more than three?
sections.label: Repeat the same method
sections.intro: Use the same distribution rule at every step. Repeated factors can be expanded early or left to the last step.

blocks.html: Treat a repeated bracket as another factor. Continue multiplying one unused factor at a time until no brackets remain.

blocks.title: Expand three or more brackets in stages
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(x + 22\right)\left(x + 22\right)\left(x - 16\right)\). Write the fully expanded result.
blocks.hint: Combine the first two brackets, then use their expanded product with the next bracket.
blocks.solution:
Expand the first two brackets. \(\left(x + 22\right)\left(x + 22\right)=x^{2} + 44 x + 484\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(x^{2} + 44 x + 484\right)\left(x - 16\right)=x^{3} + 28 x^{2} - 220 x - 7744\).

blocks.html: The leading degree helps check for a missing factor. Four non-zero linear factors give degree four.

blocks.title: Expand three or more brackets in stages
blocks.prompt: Expand and simplify \(\left(4 x + 4\right)\left(x + 21\right)\left(x - 20\right)\left(x + 1\right)\). Write the fully expanded result.
blocks.hint: Combine the first two brackets, then use their expanded product with the next bracket.
blocks.solution:
Expand the first two brackets. \(\left(4 x + 4\right)\left(x + 21\right)=4 x^{2} + 88 x + 84\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(4 x^{2} + 88 x + 84\right)\left(x - 20\right)=4 x^{3} + 8 x^{2} - 1676 x - 1680\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(4 x^{3} + 8 x^{2} - 1676 x - 1680\right)\left(x + 1\right)=4 x^{4} + 12 x^{3} - 1668 x^{2} - 3356 x - 1680\).

blocks.html: Check the leading and constant terms from the factors. Then inspect the intermediate terms.

\(- 2 y\)\(- 12 x y\)\(- 38 y^{2}\)
Read all the cells and collect like terms. \(12 x^{2}+38 x y- 12 x y- 38 y^{2}=12 x^{2} + 26 x y - 38 y^{2}\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(x^{2} + 6 x - 432\right)\left(x + 17\right)=x^{3} + 23 x^{2} - 330 x - 7344\).

Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(6 x^{2} + 144 x + 138\right)\left(2 x - 22\right)=12 x^{3} + 156 x^{2} - 2892 x - 3036\).

solution: Expand the first two brackets. \(\left(x + 23\right)\left(x + 23\right)=x^{2} + 46 x + 529\).
Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(x^{2} + 46 x + 529\right)\left(x + 17\right)=x^{3} + 63 x^{2} + 1311 x + 8993\).

examples.title: Expand three or more brackets in stages
examples.question: Expand and simplify \(\left(5 x - 5\right)\left(x + 22\right)\left(x + 21\right)\left(x + 1\right)\).
solution: Expand the first two brackets. \(\left(5 x - 5\right)\left(x + 22\right)=5 x^{2} + 105 x - 110\).
Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(5 x^{2} + 105 x - 110\right)\left(x + 21\right)=5 x^{3} + 210 x^{2} + 2095 x - 2310\).
Multiply by the next unused bracket. \(\left(5 x^{3} + 210 x^{2} + 2095 x - 2310\right)\left(x + 1\right)=5 x^{4} + 215 x^{3} + 2305 x^{2} - 215 x - 2310\).

×\(5 x\)\(5 y\)

revision.body:
Methods

StepWhat to do
Retain each algebraic partMultiply as usual. Combine the \(xy\) terms together and retain the \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) terms separately.
Expand one pair firstMultiply two brackets and simplify their product. Then multiply every term of that product by every term in the third bracket.
Repeat the same methodTreat a repeated bracket as another factor. Continue multiplying one unused factor at a time until no brackets remain.

Worked line

\((2x+y)(x-3y)=2x^2-5xy-3y^2\)

Check yourself

Expand \((x+1)(x-2)(x+3)\).

Answer \(x^3+2x^2-5x-6\)
revision.checks:
• \(x^2,xy,y^2\) are three different algebraic parts.
  • A quadratic result after the first multiplication is intermediate. One bracket is still unused.
  • The leading degree helps check for a missing factor. Four non-zero linear factors give degree four.

sections.title: How can four terms hide a repeated bracket?
sections.label: Factorise by grouping
sections.intro: Recognise a repeated group as a factor, in the same way that a repeated letter can be a factor.

blocks.html: Group two pairs. Extract a factor from each pair so an identical bracket appears twice. Then extract the whole bracket.

figure.alt: A square has a smaller corner square removed, leaving a shaded L-shaped area.
figure.caption: A large square minus a smaller square leaves an area that can be rearranged into a rectangle.

blocks.title: Factorise a repeated bracket
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully by grouping \(2 x y+25 x+14 y+175\). Enter the factor involving x first and the factor involving y second. Give each a positive leading coefficient.
blocks.hint: Look for two groups that leave identical brackets after a factor is extracted.
blocks.solution:
Arrange the terms into two groups with the same bracket left inside.

\(x\left(2 y + 25\right)+7\left(2 y + 25\right)\).

Take out that common bracket as a single factor. \(\left(x + 7\right)\left(2 y + 25\right)\).

blocks.html: \(U^2-V^2=(U+V)(U-V)\). Check that both terms already are squares and that the sign between them is a minus.

blocks.title: Factorise a difference of two squares

blocks.solution:

Use \(U^2-V^2=(U+V)(U-V)\).

The factors are \(\left(6 x + 25 y\right)\left(6 x - 25 y\right)\).

sections.title: How can I recognise a square trinomial?

blocks.html: \((U\pm V)^2=U^2\pm2UV+V^2\). The first and last squares alone are insufficient. Check the sign and size of the middle term.

blocks.title: Spot a perfect square trinomial
blocks.prompt: Factorise as a square \(64 x^{2} + 400 x y + 625 y^{2}\). Enter the bracket before squaring. Its x coefficient must be positive.
blocks.hint: Check the cross term before choosing the sign in the square.
blocks.solution:
The matching squares are \(\left(8 x\right)^2\) and \(\left(25 y\right)^2\).

The cross term must be twice the product. Here \(2\left(8 x\right)\left(25 y\right)=400 x y\).

So the factorised form is \(\left(8 x + 25 y\right)^2\).

blocks.html: The middle term must be twice the product of the square roots.

The cross term must be twice the product. Here \(2\left(6 x\right)\left(-23\right)=- 276 x\).

So the factorised form is \(\left(6 x - 23\right)^2\).

igcse-0580-manipulation-quadratic-cubic-.description: Factorise monic and non-monic quadratics, then continue after extracting a common linear factor from a suitable cubic.

sections.title: Which two constants build a monic quadratic?
sections.label: Use the required sum and product
sections.intro: A product of two monic linear factors has a cross-term equal to the sum of their constants times the variable.

blocks.html: Choose two numbers whose sum is the middle coefficient and whose product is the constant term.

figure.alt: Four original terms form two groups. Arrows lead from both groups to the same bracket.
figure.caption: Split the middle term so the two groups have a common bracket.

blocks.title: Factorise a quadratic
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully \(x^{2} + 42 x + 432\). Enter both monic brackets, with the smaller constant first. If they match, enter the same bracket twice.
blocks.hint: Extract any common factor first. For the quadratic that remains, look for a pair with the needed sum and product.
blocks.solution:
Choose constants with product \(432\) and sum \(42\). Those constants are \(18\) and \(24\).

Write the complete product. \(\left(x + 18\right)\left(x + 24\right)\).

blocks.html: A pair that has the right product but the wrong sum changes the middle term.

blocks.title: Factorise a quadratic
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully \(x^{2} - 12 x + 36\). Enter both monic brackets, with the smaller constant first. If they match, enter the same bracket twice.
blocks.hint: Extract any common factor first. For the quadratic that remains, look for a pair with the needed sum and product.
blocks.solution:
Choose constants with product \(36\) and sum \(-12\). Those constants are \(-6\) and \(-6\).

Write the complete product. \(\left(x - 6\right)\left(x - 6\right)\).

blocks.html: When the two constants match, the two factors are identical.

sections.title: What changes when the leading coefficient exceeds one?
sections.label: Split the middle term
sections.intro: The non-monic case still has two cross-products. Their product can be calculated before those cross-products are known.

blocks.html: Find two numbers whose sum is the middle coefficient and whose product is leading coefficient times constant. Split the middle term and regroup.

blocks.title: Factorise a quadratic
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully \(3 x^{2} - 52 x - 391\). Enter the two primitive linear brackets with positive coefficients of x, smaller coefficient first.
blocks.hint: Extract any common factor first. For the quadratic that remains, look for a pair with the needed sum and product.
blocks.solution:
Find the pair \(17\) and \(-69\). Their sum is \(-52\) and their product is \(-1173\).

Split the middle term, then group. \(3 x^{2}+17 x- 69 x-391=x\left(3 x + 17\right)-23\left(3 x + 17\right)\).

Write the complete product. \(\left(x - 23\right)\left(3 x + 17\right)\).

blocks.html: Using only the constant term for the target product is the monic rule. Here the leading coefficient also matters.

blocks.title: Factorise a quadratic
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully \(6 x^{2} - 29 x - 110\). Enter the two primitive linear brackets with positive coefficients of x, smaller coefficient first.
blocks.hint: Extract any common factor first. For the quadratic that remains, look for a pair with the needed sum and product.
blocks.solution:
Find the pair \(-44\) and \(15\). Their sum is \(-29\) and their product is \(-660\).

Split the middle term, then group. \(6 x^{2}- 44 x+15 x-110=2 x\left(3 x - 22\right)+5\left(3 x - 22\right)\).

Write the complete product. \(\left(2 x + 5\right)\left(3 x - 22\right)\).

blocks.html: Expand the final product to verify its leading, middle and constant terms.

sections.title: How can a cubic become a quadratic factorisation?
sections.label: Extract the common factor first
sections.intro: These cubics have no constant term. In the form considered here, taking out the common variable leaves a quadratic.

blocks.html: When every cubic term contains the variable, extract the highest common monomial factor. Then factorise the remaining quadratic if it can be split into linear factors over the integers. If no suitable split exists, leave that quadratic in one bracket.

blocks.title: Factorise a cubic with an irreducible quadratic part
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully \(24 x^{3} + 132 x^{2} + 198 x\). Give the largest common monomial with a positive coefficient, then the remaining expression.
blocks.hint: Extract the shared variable and numerical factor. Check if the remaining quadratic can be split.
blocks.solution:
The greatest common monomial factor is \(6 x\).

Dividing each term by the factor leaves \(4 x^{2} + 22 x + 33\).

For the middle-term method the two numbers must have product \(132\) and sum \(22\). The possible sums with the right sign are \(133\), \(68\), \(47\), \(37\), \(28\), \(23\).

No integer middle-term split gives both the required sum and product for this bracket. The full factorisation is \(6 x\left(4 x^{2} + 22 x + 33\right)\).

blocks.html: Stopping at a linear factor times a factorable quadratic leaves the answer incomplete.

blocks.title: Factorise a cubic with a common factor
blocks.prompt: Factorise fully \(42 x^{3} + 413 x^{2} + 770 x\). First enter the largest positive common monomial factor. Enter the two primitive linear brackets with positive coefficients of x, smaller coefficient first.
blocks.hint: Extract any common factor first. For the quadratic that remains, look for a pair with the needed sum and product.
blocks.solution:
Extract \(7 x\) to leave \(6 x^{2} + 59 x + 110\) inside the bracket.

Find the pair \(44\) and \(15\). Their sum is \(59\) and their product is \(660\).

Split the middle term, then group. \(6 x^{2}+44 x+15 x+110=2 x\left(3 x + 22\right)+5\left(3 x + 22\right)\).

Write the complete product. \(7 x\left(2 x + 5\right)\left(3 x + 22\right)\).
